real: A hot summer makes London's river so foul that Parliament literally can't work
source: 1858 — the 'Great Stink': the Thames smelled so awful during a hot dry summer that it forced Parliament to shut its windows and nearly stop sitting, accelerating the building of London's sewer system.
fakes: City council debates new cleaning contract for the river
Businesses along the waterfront report record summer trade
Scientists measure rising temperature along the Thames

real: A woman starts dancing in a market square — then hundreds join her and can't stop
source: 1518 — the Dancing Plague of Strasbourg: a woman began dancing in the street, and within a month hundreds had joined, some reportedly dancing until they collapsed from exhaustion, heart attacks, or strokes.
fakes: City officials declare a public holiday to lift spirits
Doctors prescribe a special remedy for the restless crowd
Merchants report a surge in sales near the market square

real: Two armies stand off on the border over... a single shot pig
source: 1859 — the Pig War: a brief standoff between the U.S. and Britain over the San Juan Islands, triggered when an American farmer shot a British-owned pig that had been rooting in his potato field. It never escalated to real war.
fakes: Border town braced as both nations send troops to the islands
Diplomats rush to negotiate a ceasefire at the frontier
Farmer arrested after confrontation with a rival settler

real: Two Italian cities go to war over the theft of a single bucket
source: 1631 — the War of the Bucket: a conflict between Bologna and Modena sparked, in part, by the theft of a sacred wooden bucket from Bologna's cathedral. Thousands died over a symbol.
fakes: Rival city denies involvement in the temple theft
Citizens rally to defend the city's most sacred object
Mediator proposes a truce to end the escalating feud

real: The Pope puts the corpse of his predecessor on trial — and has it burned
source: 897 — the Cadaver Synod: the mummified body of Pope Formosus was dug up, dressed in papal vestments, seated on a throne, and put on trial by his successor, who was found guilty and had the corpse mutilated and drowned.
fakes: Cardinals convene to address a disputed succession
Relics of the late pontiff are moved to a new shrine
Scholars debate the legality of the church's decision

real: Two girls take a photo of fairies — and the world's most famous skeptic believes them
source: 1917 — the Cottingley Fairies: two cousins photographed what they claimed were fairies, and the images, backed by Arthur Conan Doyle, fooled the public into believing in real fairies for decades.
fakes: Village children show off a collection of strange photos
Photographer offers to sell the images to a magazine
Local paper runs a story on an unusual family hobby

real: An unknown man spends decades gluing mysterious tiles into city streets
source: Toynbee tiles: since the 1920s, an anonymous person has embedded small ceramic tiles with a cryptic message into the streets of cities across the Americas and Australia — a mystery that has never been solved.
fakes: City workers report odd objects appearing in the pavement
Historian traces the tiles to a local artisan
Police investigate a possible hoax by a street vendor

real: The Allies float a dead man to sea with a fake invasion plan sewn into his briefcase
source: 1943 — Operation Mincemeat: British intelligence used a dead body, posed as a Royal Marines officer carrying forged documents, to fool Germany about the true target of the Allied invasion of Italy.
fakes: Naval intelligence uncovers a spy network in neutral waters
Officials dispose of a body found floating near the coast
War room scrambles to verify a suspicious map

real: Nine hikers die on a snowy mountain under conditions that defy every explanation
source: 1959 — the Dyatlov Pass incident: nine experienced Soviet hikers died on the Ural mountains under mysterious circumstances, their tent cut from the inside and bodies scattered, spawning decades of theories.
fakes: Rescue team launches search after hikers fail to check in
Investigators reconstruct the group's route through the snow
Local villagers report seeing strange lights on the ridge

real: An army base in England reports repeated sightings of a 'craft' on a foggy forest
source: 1980 — the Rendlesham Forest incident: U.S. Air Force personnel stationed in Suffolk, England, reported multiple encounters with an unexplained object in a forest, calling it 'the closest thing to a UFO experience' they had seen.
fakes: Airmen report unusual lights during a night training exercise
Base security investigates a series of break-ins near the woods
Officials deny rumors of a secret military facility in the area

real: A 600-year-old book is written in a language no one can read — even today
source: The Voynich manuscript: a 15th-century illustrated codex written in an unknown script and language. Despite centuries of attempts by cryptographers, no one has been able to decode it.
fakes: Museum acquires a rare medieval text of unknown origin
Linguists struggle to identify the script of an old codex
Auction house lists a priceless book at record prices

real: A ship is found sailing with its engine running — and not a single soul on board
source: The Mary Celeste: discovered adrift in the Atlantic in 1872 with the cargo intact and food still on the table, but the entire crew of 10 missing. Their fate was never explained.
fakes: Rescue vessel discovers a drifting boat with no crew aboard
Mariners report a storm that scattered several ships
Investigators search for the missing sailors' last known port

real: A man jumps from a plane with $200,000 in cash — and is never found again
source: 1971 — D.B. Cooper: a man who called himself Dan Cooper hijacked a Boeing 737, took $200,000 in ransom, and parachuted out over the Pacific Northwest. He was never found.
fakes: Airlines tighten security after a passenger's unusual demand
FBI launches a nationwide search for a missing hijacker
Authorities ask the public for tips on the mysterious man

real: Two children appear in an English village with green skin — and speak no one's language
source: The Green Children of Woolpit: a 12th-century legend in which two children, one with green skin, appeared in the village of Woolpit speaking an unknown language, and their origin is still debated.
fakes: Villagers take in two lost children found at the forest edge
Priest struggles to communicate with the strange newcomers
Local lord offers a reward for the children's missing family

real: Dutch traders pay the price of a house for a single flower bulb
source: 1637 — Tulip mania: in the Dutch Republic, tulip bulb prices skyrocketed to the value of a house before crashing, becoming the first recorded speculative bubble in financial history.
fakes: Flower markets report record demand for rare bulbs
Traders argue over the true value of a prized bloom
Merchants warn of overheating in the horticulture trade
